_comment: Machine health watch thresholds (docs/health-watch.md). Re-read on every sample, so a retune needs no restart.
Process rules: a value past watch_value/act_value, or steady growth past watch_rate_per_hour/act_rate_per_hour once the value is at least rate_min_value. null disables a limit.
memory_mb has no absolute limit: a model server legitimately holds tens of GB; only steady growth is judged.
System rules: watch/act limits; below=true means a low value is the bad one.
Handles are file descriptors on macOS/Linux; commit and pool counters exist only on Windows.

resource: the one-minute RAM / free-disk / per-disk latency watch with Telegram alerts (docs/health-watch.md). A sample is one minute, so sustain_samples is minutes. alert_below / alert_above_ms are the limits; min_ios is the fewest operations a window must complete to be judged for latency. disk_load: a physical disk that is busy, queued and slow all at once for the sustained samples is watch, then alert. alert.script null = ~/.claude/hooks/notify_send.py.

ports: the 30 s port watch (docs/health-watch.md). tcp_percent / udp_percent are the share of each protocol's dynamic range in use, judged on the worst sample in hold_minutes. A Tcpip 4231/4266 event in the System log is act for event_hold_hours; a 4227 is watch unless port use around it was at the act line. The burst window tallies every window_interval_s while the newest sample reaches window_arm_percent of either range (or no fresh sample says otherwise), every window_idle_interval_s below it. window_confirm_percent is the share of a range one process must rise by inside the window to be named the holder of a Tcpip 4231/4266 event; a smaller rise is reported as the largest rise, too small to exhaust the range.
